featured_reviews.name: Ishaan Srivastav
featured_reviews.review_text: We had the pleasure of taking the inside CSMT (Crown Jewel of Mumbai) tour with Sarthak Mahajan, and he was exceptional. Sarthak is incredibly knowledgeable, seamlessly weaving together stories of the building’s storied past with insights into its present-day operations. His passion for the history of the station is evident, and he made the entire walk a very pleasant, fun and engaging experience. Highly recommended for anyone looking to truly understand the soul of this UNESCO World Heritage site!

featured_reviews.name: Carol Thomson
featured_reviews.review_text:
The CST tour was a great experience.
It really felt like stepping into a whole different world full of history and amazing architecture.

Our guide, Sarthak, was exceptional. He eloquently walked us through the evolution of Indian Railways and the fascinating story behind CST, bringing every detail to life.
He also took us to all the best spots, which made it even better.

The architecture is just beautiful and so diverse—you can really see why it’s a UNESCO World Heritage site.

Overall, it was a memorable time and I’m really grateful to Sarthak for all the insights and knowledge that he shared.

featured_reviews.name: Samar Devdass
featured_reviews.review_text:
Loved the grand heritage walk of CSMT station. Very well conducted tour. Our tour guide Sarthak Mahajan was warm and welcoming. Taking us around in an easy pace allowing us to soke-in every moment.

Though the property is a UNESCO World heritage site, it is in a very bad state of up-keep, especially the interiors. If we don't take care of it now it will just wither away. We are answerable to the next generation. Looking forward to more such tours. Thanks

featured_reviews.name: Trupti Rane
featured_reviews.review_text:
Today i.e. 17/01/26, I attended The Crown Jewel of Mumbai - Inside CSMT tour hosted by Ms. Shravani of Raconteur tours, it was a wonderful experience.
Very well explained by the host Ms. Shravani with very detailed information about our Railway history n CSMT Building structure.

Would highly recommend this tour to everyone and can be added as one of the visit places in itinerary for Mumbai.

Wishing all the best to host n the tour agency.

Best regards,
Trupti Rane

featured_reviews.name: Huda Dalwai
featured_reviews.review_text: Wonderful experience, lots of fun. Our guide Shravani was very knowledgeable and kind. She answered all our questions and made the tour very interactive. Giving her a five star as well!!!!

featured_reviews.name: dhanwanti rajwade
featured_reviews.review_text: We went with two kids, aged 13 and 10 for the Crown Jewel of India walk with Pankaj. He was an outstanding guide! He engaged all age groups, was patient, was entertaining and had a real passion for the subject, which was evident in his delivery. I would love to go for many more walks with him, and highly recommend this experience for anyone in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: E Marbach
featured_reviews.review_text: What a great time we had with Sarthak. He knew so much about the railway and we had really good discussions with him about India and Britain and rail history and architecture. It was really worth going to the station with a guide. It brought it all to life and we noticed more than we ever would have.

featured_reviews.name: Binki Gundavda
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited with my relatives from London as tourists...on 20 th Jan.2026 Tuesday. The crown jewel of Mumbai. Inside CSMT tour.
It was an awesome experience, a very proud feeling too of our heritage culture and values...got lots of detailed and minute information from our tour guide Mr. Sarthak, he is a very friendly person, with perfect knowledge of his subject and he could answer queries of other tourists and ours too very smoothly and clearly...he threw light on so many minute details which I was not aware of as a Mumbaikar...
I suggest that everyone must take this tour once, as a tourist to learn more about our very own heritage culture and values and places.

name: Zamorin of Bombay | Walking Cultural and City Tours in Mumbai
description:
Zamorin of Bombay, founded in June 2015, is a Value and Experience based Tour Company & specializes in connecting the tourist and the local through tours and experiences based on value and connect. Embark on a journey that unveils the city's soul from the lively markets where colours and aromas converge to the tranquil fishing villages where tradition meets the sea.
Our expert guides will lead you through the vibrant city covering gems both on and off the beaten track, showcasing the authentic spirit of Mumbai.

Whether you're a history buff, a culture connoisseur, or a traveler seeking authenticity, we at Zamorin of Bombay promise an enriching experience that will make you fall in love with our city.

owner.name: Zamorin of Bombay | Walking Cultural and City Tours in Mumbai (Owner)

featured_reviews.name: Jutta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Best tour guide ever!
If you want to experience Mumbai like a local, really be part of the experience rather than a bystander, get in touch with the locals and discover Mumbai in a fun and interactive way, Viren is the guide to go with! He knows basically everything about his city and the people and shares his knowledge with wit and passion.
Whether you want to visit the highlights of Mumbai or go completely off the beaten track, Viren can customize your tour according to your preferences.
Thanks again for the amazing time!

featured_reviews.name: Duran- Franks
featured_reviews.review_text: This was my first time to India and I was able to add a little extra time to explore in Mumbai. I’m so glad a friend recommended Viren! Over the 1 1/2 days we had together I learned a TON about the history, culture, architecture and foreign influences of the area. We saw a sixth century cave temple, the slums, the harbor, a vibrant market - and many places off the beaten path. Viren is a wealth of information and a lot of fun - highly recommend!!

featured_reviews.name: Nive Raitz von Frentz
featured_reviews.review_text:
I came to know Viren DSa through our school walking group and have done several walks with him.  Highlights include a recent half day exploration of Vasai Fort, which he facilitated with another guide.  We travelled by local train and tuktuks, spending two wonderful hours roaming the fortress ruins.  Highly recommended.

Across the Dadar markets, all the way to the art deco buildings of Shivaji Park, ending with a stunning view of the Sea Link was another excellent walk.  Meandering through the narrow lanes of Kothachiwadi and the Worli Koliwada were equally enjoyable experiences.

Viren does know his history and peppers his talks with anecdotes on colourful local customs.  Friendly and polite, it has been an interesting experience arranging walks with him.  He sometimes gets carried away as he has so many stories to tell!

featured_reviews.name: Atul Katdare
featured_reviews.review_text:
Highly Recommended Tours in Bombay & around..

Viren, one of the most passionate & knowledgeable tour leader I met yesterday during the Heritage Walk to Vasai Fort. it was a perfect tour & Viren had an answer to almost everything 😄 History, Culture, Religions, Languages & lot more.. I just loved the the way he curated this walk & his narratives were pretty much impressive. He made the tour engaging by telling interesting trivia & interactive by sharing humorous jokes.😜 I'm glad we met (finally)! It was one of the best collaboration #Bhovara had at the beginning of this year. Thanks a lot for this wonderful experience & pleasant memories. Hope to see u again very soon..

I strongly suggest everyone to experience Heritage in & around Bombay city through Viren's vision. It's worth a walk wid zamorin of bombay tours

featured_reviews.name: Francoise Roncey
featured_reviews.review_text: Viren was a fantastic guide through Mumbai! He brought me to neighborhoods that are less touristy and personalized the itinerary based on my preferences. I spent a fabulous time visiting Mumbai thanks to him :) I 100% recommend him for your next trip to India!

featured_reviews.name: Harshad Kapadia
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the most meticulous and detailed tour I have ever had in my life, within Mumbai.The commentry during the walking tour was so interested that we didn't realise when it ended.
In fact, inspite of staying in South Mumbai,I never knew of South Mumbai so much in details which I learned during my walking tour.
One must never miss the wonderful,amazing knowledge filled experience while you are in Mumbai, India.

featured_reviews.name: Sheherazad Pavri
featured_reviews.review_text: Viren will regale you with his stories and give you a unique experience that you don't want to miss when exploring the city. Hes multilingual and will keep you comfortable while also taking you on an adventure 😀

featured_reviews.name: Lorraine Agyar
featured_reviews.review_text: Very detailed informative tour. The tour guide Viren goes all out his way to create a wonderful experience and gives you a one of a kind tour.

featured_reviews.name: Andrea Gomes
featured_reviews.review_text: I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude to Beyond Heritage for organizing such an enriching heritage walk at Colaba. The walk was incredibly informative, offering not only a deep dive into the architectural marvels of the area but also providing valuable insights into the present state and history of the neighborhood. The passion and knowledge shared by them made this experience truly memorable. I highly recommend their walks to anyone looking to explore and learn more about the rich heritage around us. Thank you for an unforgettable experience!

featured_reviews.name: Paru C
featured_reviews.review_text: Fort-O-Frame Photwalk conducted by Beyond Heritage was one of the best that I have ever attended. It was very informative giving lots of details about the history of Bombay. (now Mumbai) Would recommend it to all those who are keen to learn about this city!

featured_reviews.name: Kalpak Raut
featured_reviews.review_text: An amazing walk with great insights from Raunak and Mallika. I have always loved to know the history behind heritage. The walk is so well curated that it presents the heritage with little pieces of history that will remain with you for a long time.

featured_reviews.name: Suyash Nadkarni
featured_reviews.review_text: Got a glimpse into Mumbai’s architecture and bustling markets, all thanks to Malika from Beyond Heritage. We, my husband and I started out early in the wee hours to experience the buzz at Dadar flower and vegetable wholesale markets. Malika shared lots of informative insights regarding the architecture- central library and the buildings in and around it of historic significance. Thanks for making it enjoyable and interesting, Malika Keer! 👌

featured_reviews.name: SUJITH AIL
featured_reviews.review_text:
Did a Bombay heritage tour with Mallika.
A well organised event with lots of insights with a very inclusive vibe. Hoping to go for many more walks with Beyond Heritage

featured_reviews.name: Santa C (Santa C)
featured_reviews.review_text: Malika is a great tour guide. Detailed knowledge of Mumbai through the eyes of a heritage architect. Safe driver and an excellent host.

featured_reviews.name: Trupti Tawde
featured_reviews.review_text:
Walking the esplanades with Beyond Heritage gave me a new appreciation for the city's history.
The 'Bombay Beyond Fort' tour was insightful and revealed architectural details I had missed before.
Thank you for a wonderful morning exploring the heart of old Bombay.

featured_reviews.name: Eesha Nopany
featured_reviews.review_text: Mallika is an expert in her field of architecture. She took a group of 10 of us around South Mumbai while sharing stories from the past, answering all our questions, and keeping the information super easy to absorb while sharing her knowledge! She is amazing to work with and would highly recommend one of her walks to get to know Mumbai a little bit better in a fun way!

name: IanWalksMumbai
description:
IanWalksMumbai is your invitation to discover the city the way Ian did—on foot, with curiosity, humor, and a healthy respect for potholes. Expect vivid histories, unexpected detours, and probably a snack stop or three. You won’t just see Mumbai—you’ll feel it, taste it, laugh with it… and maybe get a little lost with Ian (on purpose).

Ready to walk? Let’s go.

featured_reviews.name: Cassandra R
featured_reviews.review_text: I booked a full day tour with Ian and couldn’t have had a better guide to show me all over Mumbai. He was on time, curated my experience to my tastes, so full of information, and a welcoming host. He met me at my hotel, arranged for a driver, sweated in 43°, and never slowed down. I tasted food safely, felt safe as a solo woman traveler, never felt forced into buying anything I didn’t. It was truly an experience of a lifetime and I’m so very grateful. Thank you Ian!

featured_reviews.name: An G
featured_reviews.review_text:
We went for a heritage walk in CSMT with Ian late-September, and it was a blast!

He’s energetic, well-informed and convivial!

The walk took about 2 hours — wherein we explored the exterior and interior architectural aspects of the iconic train station. Throughout the walk, Ian regaled us with stories of historical significance, and even quizzed us a bit along the way! It was very engaging.

We made a stop at the train museum inside the station - a modest setup with a LOT of paraphernalia for rail transport enthusiasts!

Before we did this walk - We really didn’t know how much the station had to offer, despite living in Mumbai for some time now.

Walks like these are a lovely way to get acquainted with the city. An experience made all the richer with an enthusiastic and passionate guide like Ian!

We look forward to joining him for another heritage walk sometime! Thank you for a memorable time.

featured_reviews.name: Manmohan Patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Really enjoyed the CSMT UNESCO World Heritage Tour! Ian was an amazing guide super friendly and knew so many cool facts about the place. The way he explained the history and little details made it really interesting. Had a great time exploring and learning. Totally worth it! 😊

featured_reviews.name: Obada
featured_reviews.review_text: We took an evening tour fir the south of Mumbai. The trip with Ian was very informative, engaging and interesting. Ian has a fun story telling style that makes the tour special. The fact that it's a private free walking tour is really unique and offers a lot of flexibility in terms of the tour's timing and topics in focus. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.name: Rajdeep Maity
featured_reviews.review_text: I've visited CSMT countless times growing up, but I never really understood its architecture until this tour. Seeing it through Ian's explanation changed the entire experience. The way you broke things down made the details easy to follow, and the way you told the stories behind the place kept it engaging instead of feeling like a history lecture. I walked away actually appreciating the structure instead of just passing by it. Overall, the tour was genuinely fun and surprisingly eye-opening

featured_reviews.name: Ananya Nayak
featured_reviews.review_text:
On Saturday, 6th of December I took a tour of CSMT with Ian. When I had booked the tour (available in BMS) I was only interested in the gigantic magnificent buildings. But Ian, made me look and understand them. This person is nostalgic and passionate about the history and buildings. He not only recites the history, he connects the dots to the present.

He quizzes you on things, makes it interactive and introspective and is very friendly. He narrates fun incidents happening over different times and isn't afraid to admit that there are few things that he isn't very aware of.

The walk is designed to have a look at almost everything, including a reclusive Railway Museum which isn't other wise opened to the public. He also recommends other tours, areas to explore and much more.

I would definitely recommend this tour.

featured_reviews.name: Krishnan Anantharaman
featured_reviews.review_text: Ian led our tour of CSMT in Mumbai, including areas of the grand railway office building that are off limits to the public. He kept the tour fun and engaging, and covered a LOT of ground in a short time: colonial history, architecture, commerce and all the other influences on this spectacular structure.

featured_reviews.name: Ajit Varma
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a very interesting and informative tour in which the history and architectural aspects of the CSMT building is explained very minutely. There is also a heritage railway museum visit in this having lots of interesting information on past present railway. One can also see working models.
Our tour guide was Mr Ian Fernandes. He is extremely talented and good communicator.
He took special care for senior citizens.
Well priced and value for money tour.
One who is visiting Mumbai should go for this.
We booked on  Bookmy show app .Tour name is "crown jewel of Mumbai inside CSMT".

featured_reviews.name: Howard Kaplan
featured_reviews.review_text:
we did the essential Mumbai tour with Parvez. he was a great guide for a great trip. The tour started off near the Asiatic society, and we walked around the area originally inside the Fort walls. He helped create a wonderful imagery of what the city looked like when it was founded along with some stories about the history before hand that led up to establishing Mumbai.
The trip was a mixture of walking and getting in and out of a car to see various sites around the city. It was quite varied and allowed us to see some unusual sites we would not have seen by ourselves.
at the end of the tour, we stopped at a restaurant with Parvez and tried several dishes that were excellent. Common food that is regularly served in restaurants, but this was delicious.

If this was representative of the companies tou, I would strongly recommend them for a tour.

featured_reviews.name: Varun Khandka
featured_reviews.review_text:
This afternoon we went for a heritage walk of the BMC office. We randomly signed up for this, thought its better to do something rather than just sitting home, but this was so much more than just "something".
We met Mr. Mickey, who led the walk, such an amazing, lively and knowledgeable guy. He kept the whole walk so engaging, the way he explained us about the things was truly outstanding. This was one of the best things to experience in Mumbai, we have already planned to do the fort walk and we are definitely going to sign up for more with Khaki Tours.

featured_reviews.name: Chirag
featured_reviews.review_text:
Must do -- even if you are a local!

We have been to the Fort area multiple times and while we have driven past the monuments multiple times, we never observed them!

Walking tour with Khakhi, helped us see the details that we have never noticed, heard stories that we did not know and helped us appreciate the history behind the buildings.

Our tour guide (Omkar) was very patient (especially with our 9 year old) and knowledgeable. He gave us a detailed tour and explained the nuances.

I would highly recommend this tour to anyone who wants to know about the history of Mumbai

featured_reviews.name: Sandy D
featured_reviews.review_text:
Did the Essential Mumbai tour with Sagar Joshi from Khaki Tours, and he was an excellent guide, storyteller, and truly passionate about Mumbai.

It was brutally hot the day we took the tour, but Sagar was patient, engaging, and took the time to explain everything in detail. Highly recommended for anyone wanting to experience and understand Mumbai beyond the usual tourist spots.

featured_reviews.name: Tejal Samant
featured_reviews.review_text: We visited the BMC Headquarters with Khaki Tours on 25th May, and it was an absolutely awesome experience! The heritage architecture of the building is simply stunning — a true gem in the heart of Mumbai. Every Mumbaikar should and must visit this iconic place to appreciate the city's rich history and civic pride. Our tour guide, Juzer Tambawalla, was incredibly knowledgeable and engaging, bringing the stories of this magnificent structure to life. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: P K
featured_reviews.review_text: We had arranged for a group tour of Castle 2 Gateway through Khakee Tour. It was the best experience we ever had. We had 55 people in group most of them born and bought up in Mumbai. But we didnt knew even 10% history and facts of what they showed and explained us. We had 3 sub groups but everybody had excellent experience with their guides. Our tour guide was Parag who was fabulous. His passion for Mumbai was evident. A must do tour for every mumbaikar

featured_reviews.name: Max Mackie
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mumbai history comes alive! An amazing walk with Surabhi.

I recently took the Fort area heritage walk with Khaki Tours, and I cannot recommend it enough. Our guide, Surabhi, was absolutely fantastic.
It wasn’t just a recitation of dates and facts; Surabhi is a natural storyteller. She wove together the history of colonial Bombay with fascinating anecdotes about the architecture and the people who built this city. She pointed out hidden details in the Gothic buildings that I would have walked right past without noticing.

Her energy was contagious, and she was incredibly patient in answering all our questions. Whether you are a tourist or a local Mumbaikar, you will see the Fort area with completely new eyes after this. If you book a Khaki Tour, definitely ask for Surabhi!

featured_reviews.name: Kay V
featured_reviews.review_text: A must experience tour for those who want to know rich heritage of Mumbai. We took a corporate package for women's day. Since it was March and the walking tour is of two hours, I feel they should introduce early morning slots starting at 7 instead of 8. Almost ll of us felt tired due to heat and despite having water bottles with us.  Guides were knowledgeable nd cordial. The guides are working in corporate or in private sectors. The individual's volunteer for these tours aa guides. They have lots of packages as per your needs. We took  a heritage walk package for Girgaum

featured_reviews.name: Mark Stephenson
featured_reviews.review_text:
Everything was amazing from start to finish! The booking process with Sam was seamless—he helped us choose the perfect tours for our two days in Mumbai. From the moment we arrived, we were warmly welcomed at the airport by Shamsher, our driver. His safe and careful driving made us feel completely comfortable throughout the journey.

And then there was Aryan, our tour guide—what an absolute star! His knowledge was outstanding, and spending time with him was a real pleasure. He brought the city to life in a way that was both engaging and unforgettable.

I honestly can’t recommend this company enough. The value for money was incredible, and the entire experience exceeded our expectations. Don’t hesitate—book with this incredible company and you’ll be in the best hands!

featured_reviews.name: Michael Porter
featured_reviews.review_text:
An Unforgettable and Eye Opening Tour with the Amazing Pooja!

Our tour of Dharavi with Magical Mumbai Tour was one of the absolute highlights of our time in the city, and it was made truly special by our fantastic guide, Pooja.
From the very beginning, Pooja was warm, knowledgeable, and incredibly passionate. She didn't just show us the sights; she shared stories and introduced us to the vibrant community spirit that makes Dharavi so unique. Her personal connection to the area allowed for an authentic and respectful experience that completely shattered our preconceptions. We learned so much about the recycling businesses, the local industries, and the daily lives of the resilient and hardworking people who live there.
If you are thinking about taking this tour, we cannot recommend it enough. For the best possible experience, you MUST ask for Pooja. Her insight, professionalism, and wonderful personality are what made this a five-star, truly unforgettable tour!

featured_reviews.name: Rosie Payavlas
featured_reviews.review_text:
Highly Recommended Dharavi Tour with Sneha

We had an excellent tour of Dharavi with Sneha — she’s an incredibly knowledgeable and engaging guide who gave us deep insight into the community. She took us through the commercial areas, including plastic recycling, soap making, and small workshops, and explained each process clearly. We also visited locations featured in Slumdog Millionaire, as well as local schools, chicken shops, and leather goods makers. Sneha clearly understands the area, its people, and their resilience. Highly recommend this eye-opening and respectful experience!

featured_reviews.name: Daisy Rhea Dharwadkar
featured_reviews.review_text: I had a wonderful experience exploring Mumbai with our tour guide Neha and driver Dildar. They were very professional, friendly, and made sure we were comfortable throughout the trip. Neha explained everything clearly and gave us great insights into the city’s culture and history(even through all the rain). Dildar was careful and reliable, making the travel smooth and stress-free. Overall, it was a memorable experience, and I would highly recommend them to anyone visiting Mumbai!

featured_reviews.name: Christopher Teale
featured_reviews.review_text: Did a Mumbai city guided bicycle tour starting at 6am- it was really good. The roads were really quiet and it was lovely and cool. Our guide was Sahil who spoke great English, was knowledgable and really interesting.  We visited the fish market and outdoor laundry and able to see these places at their busiest time. We saw other interesting places in the city. I highly recommend this tour.

featured_reviews.name: Ellie Hartley
featured_reviews.review_text: An amazing tour of the slums with Pooja! She was so funny and interesting. A great tour. I would definitely recommend it!! We also went on the Mumbai day tour Atik and JQ who were both amazing too. The driving was very safe and a cool car. Atik our guide was so knowledgeable and answered all our questions with great answers and in perfect English

featured_reviews.name: Shivani Darji
featured_reviews.review_text: We had a great experience with this tour company even though we booked with them on short notice. The manager was responsive and answered all of the questions we had along with helping to identify where a discount can be applied for Indian document holders, which was appreciative. We did the Elephanta Caves tour and the local tour guide we were paired up with there through Magical Mumbai Tours did a fantastic job explaining the detailed history behind the caves and scupltures and gave us plenty of time for photos. It was a really hot day but he still explained everything with a smile and elaborated where we asked questions. Would refinitely recommend this tour company! They also have women tour guides!

featured_reviews.name: stephen ng
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a fantastic private sightseeing tour of Mumbai with Shuaib. He shared many local insights into the lives of Mumbai's residents, adding depth and context to the city's vibrant culture.

The tour was comfortable, with a private car and personalized attention throughout. It's a great option if you want to see the highlights of Mumbai in just half a day. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Shivaji Park is not just a ground — it’s an emotion for every cricket lover. If you really want to watch future superstars of Indian cricket in the making, this is the place to be. On the red soil of this historic ground, you’ll see young kids practicing with full dedication, sweating it out under the sharp Mumbai sun, chasing their dreams with bat and ball in hand.
There’s something special about standing there and watching them play. The sound of leather hitting the bat, coaches shouting instructions, and parents cheering from the side — it all feels raw and real. Many legends, including Sachin Tendulkar, began their journey here, which makes the atmosphere even more inspiring.
The park is huge, so even if you're not into cricket, it’s a perfect place for a peaceful walk or to just sit and relax. In the evening, the cool breeze and open space make it ideal for clearing your mind after a long day.
And of course, no visit is complete without trying the famous vada pav near Shivaji Park. The street food around the area is amazing — simple, authentic, and full of Mumbai flavor. Grabbing a hot vada pav after watching an intense practice session just feels right.

The street food stalls are a whole emotion — from classic Mumbai snacks to quick bites, everything tastes better when you’re walking around with your people. 😋

Love how the place has something for everyone — kids playing cricket, fitness lovers using the open gym, elders enjoying their walks, and youngsters just chilling and soaking in the atmosphere.

And the best part? The crowd. It’s not just a park, it’s a cultural heartbeat of Mumbai. You’ll see real, raw Mumbai here — diverse, energetic, and full of life. ❤️

featured_reviews.name: Amit Gurav
featured_reviews.review_text: Shivaji Park, officially Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park, is a public park situated in Dadar, Mumbai. It is the largest park in the island city. Similar but bigger in size to Azad Maidan and August Kranti Maidan (formerly Gowalia Tank Grounds), it is of historical and cultural value because of the political and social gatherings it has witnessed, both in pre- and post-independence Mumbai. The 113,000 square metres (28 acres) of open space is renowned as having been a cradle of the game of cricket in India.

featured_reviews.name: Ayaj Deshmukh
featured_reviews.review_text:
🌿 A Majestic Experience at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park
🏞️ Pride of Dadar, Mumbai | A Historic Ground of Courage & Culture 👑🇮🇳
Visiting Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park in Dadar, Mumbai, was a truly memorable, emotional, and inspiring experience for me 💚. This park is not just an open ground—it is a historical landmark that carries the spirit of Maharashtra’s pride, unity, and rich legacy 🌟. The moment I stepped onto this vast green land, I felt a deep sense of respect and belonging 🙏.
The park is named after Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, the great Maratha warrior king who symbolizes bravery, good governance, and Swarajya 👑⚔️. Standing here, I could feel the echoes of history in the air. This ground has witnessed many historic political movements, social gatherings, freedom-related events, and public speeches that shaped modern Maharashtra 🇮🇳📜. Knowing this made my visit even more meaningful and powerful.
As I walked through the park, I noticed people of all ages—children playing, elders walking peacefully, students practicing sports, and groups doing yoga 🏃‍♂️🧘‍♀️. The park beautifully balances history and daily life, showing how the past and present coexist harmoniously 🌸. The lush greenery and open space provide a refreshing escape from the busy city life of Mumbai 🌳🌬️.
One of the most emotional aspects of my visit was realizing that this very ground has been a platform for voices demanding justice, equality, and rights ✊. Many great leaders have addressed the nation from here, making it a silent witness to India’s democratic journey 🗣️📢. Being present at such a historically significant place filled me with pride and responsibility as a citizen 🤍.
The surrounding area reflects Mumbai’s cultural richness, with nearby temples, roads filled with local life, and a strong sense of Maharashtrian identity 🎭🪔. The park stands as a reminder that public spaces can unite people beyond caste, religion, and background, just like the ideals of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj himself 🤝.
As the evening breeze touched my face and the sky slowly changed colors 🌅, I felt calm yet energized. This place doesn’t just relax the body—it awakens the soul. It teaches us discipline, unity, and respect for our roots 🌱.
In conclusion, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park is more than a park—it is a living chapter of Indian history 🏞️📖. Every visit deepens respect for our heritage and inspires us to live with courage, integrity, and love for the nation 🚩✨.

featured_reviews.name: Raza
featured_reviews.review_text:
There’s something about Dadar Chowpatty that just feels like home. It’s not 'fancy' like some of the other beaches, but that’s exactly why I love it.
I came here last Tuesday after a really long day at work, and honestly, it was exactly what I needed. I just sat on the sand for an hour, watched the waves, and looked at the Sea Link glowing in the distance. It’s one of those rare places in Mumbai where you can actually hear your own thoughts.
I ended up chatting with an old uncle who’s been coming here for 30 years, and he told me the beach has its own rhythm. You see families laughing, couples holding hands, and students stressed about exams—all just co-existing.
A few 'human' tips if you go:
• The Chana Chor Garam: Get a cone from the guy near the entrance. It’s the perfect salty snack for a walk.
• The Rocks: Be careful if you sit on the tetrapods! They’re great for photos, but they can be slippery.
• The Timing: Go right when the sun is dipping. The sky turns this incredible shade of pink and orange that no camera can really catch.
If you’re feeling a bit overwhelmed by the city pace, come here. Buy a kulfi, kick off your shoes, and just exist for a bit. It’s good for the soul. ❤️

featured_reviews.name: Liviu-Alexandru Buftea (Style)
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you found this place, you had a good guide!

I thought it was Portuguese, but it's actually British. Black as the basaltic rock that rises from the sea, Worli Fort gives a great overview of the bay and the city. It features the classic crenelations and ramparts of the 17th century, and guards the golf from the tip of this tongue of land.

The fort now is not officially maintained or "open to the public". In fact, it seems even locals don’t know about it, but my friend brought me here cause she heard it’s nice. It is accessible for explorer types, and is basically left abandoned.

The fort is simply used by people in this neighborhood for storage, hang out, kids play space, etc. Some clothes left out to dry on the sides, and some barrels and stuff in the rooms below.

Here we met a couple of guys from the city, chilling, listening to cool music, they welcomed us to chat.

It smelled of sea salt, soap, garbage, fish and rats, and the breeze brought “fresh” air from the sea.

As a first time visitor in India, I was in culture shock. Seeing everything was kind of like a dreamy, surreal landscape. So I probably romanticized it too much, for the place is a slum surrounded by a garbage dump, and people here have little chance to better their days, but they were happy, kind and curious.

It was an interesting and humbling experience, worth respect.

featured_reviews.name: Derishta Pillay
featured_reviews.review_text:
At the outset I must say that neither myself nor my husband are huge fans of the usual guided walking tours mainly because we hate being taken to cliched and crowded tourist hotspots, listening to facts straight from the Wikipedia page and jostling for space with other tourists just to return sunburned and underwhelmed. In addition we'd already spent a hectic 5 weeks in India - we were tired, grumpy, waiting to fly back home and not at all looking forward to our last 4 days in Mumbai at all. So basically when our travel companions insisted we book a tour - the scene was set for disaster...
'Bombay Walks' single handedly turned this around and Mumbai actually turned out to be the highlight of our trip! (Nope this is not a sponsored review 😂)

The tour: Arpan's tour extends to the days before and after the actual tour as he offers valuable advice about where to stay/eat/party/shop etc. He speaks perfect English, is pleasant and very easy to communicate with. His passion and love for the city is infectious and you will end his tour enthralled, overwhelmed and completely charmed by Mumbai and it's people - vowing to come back and dig deeper, spend longer and see more. The city tour covers many facets of the city - traveling to hidden gems and local landmarks across the length and breadth of Mumbai. You get to see and experience aspects of Mumbai that you'd never be able to do alone with a guide book or google maps - like traveling on local trains and walking through Worli fishing village and stopping by at small off-the-beaten path temples and churches.

The guide: Arpan is reliable, trustworthy and comes well prepared for the type of group. His talking style is light-hearted and easy going but still knowledgeable and always engaging. He's the type of guide that can tell you interesting facts about the history, architecture and politics of a place but also where to get the best coconut water along the way and which public toilets are ok to use.
We only met Arpan in person on the day of the tour and although we were constantly bombarded with sights, sounds and smells (it is Mumbai after all) - it never once felt like we were just being dragged from point to point whilst he rattled off information but rather that we were spending the day walking around with an old friend.

Target travelers: We're fairly well travelled and yet this is the first time we've ever bothered to leave a tour review - on any platform - I think that in itself indicates how highly we recommend this tour.
This is really a 'must do' in Mumbai.
It's so good we would do this tour again even if it were to cover the exact route we already took. The walking wasn't particular strenuous so it's recommended for any age group it should also be noted that we found that     Arpan was discreetly always conscious of where the group members were and their safety and constantly aware of our surroundings and the locals around us - on that note I would recommend this tour even if you're a single female traveling alone.

When to do it: Try and do this tour on your first full day in Mumbai because it's also a great way to orientate yourself around the city and plan the rest of your time there.

That city that everyone talks about - that's all of India's many faces and layers in one, that accepts everyone, that's everyone's home - regardless of language, religion or creed - Mumbai is THAT city and you'd be crazy if you miss the opportunity to let a born-and-bred local guide you around...

featured_reviews.name: Jyoti Jaiswar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Took a peaceful forest walk and honestly loved the vibe 🌿✨
The entry ticket is just ₹25 per person — booking in advance is a smart idea. The trail has a charming wooden bridge and is surrounded by lush greenery, making the whole walk feel calm and refreshing. The trees are neatly labelled, which adds a nice learning touch. Plus, you get a beautiful glimpse of Girgaon Chowpatty from up there.
A perfect little escape for anyone who enjoys quiet nature moments.

featured_reviews.name: Roslin Dwivedi
featured_reviews.review_text: It’s a great place to enjoy nature, with quietness and stunning sea views. Spotting birds and learning their names and plant names is fun also it’s written on metal plates in some places on the hand railings. The walking bridge is not very long if you think you are going to walk here. It’s a place you can admire nature. The tickets you can buy on their online website of Brihan Mumbai is 50 Rs for Indians and 100 Rs for tourists. Snacks and drinks are not appreciated here. Morning slots for the visit are the best if you don’t want crowds.

featured_reviews.name: Anupam Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text: It's shorter than what I'd expected. You can complete the entire walk in half hour if you walk at a very leisurely pace. It's worth it though because the trail is really good and very well maintained. The walkway is narrow so the crowds are correctly regulated. You can even catch the sun over Marine Drive so its possibly a great place to watch the sunrise. Much needed addition to Mumbai's tourist spots and a great companion to the neighbouring parks.

featured_reviews.name: Jogendra Meena
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited the Forest Walkway in Malabar Hills around 3 PM, right in the heart of August when the monsoon is at its most vibrant. The moment we stepped in, the earthy fragrance of rain‑kissed trees and the soothing greenery set the tone for a peaceful afternoon.

Walking along the pathway with my better half was genuinely delightful. The walkway itself is about 400 metres one way—beautiful, but it left us wishing for more. If it were extended to around a kilometre on each side, and if the boundaries were designed to offer complete privacy from the outside world, the experience would have felt even more immersive, almost like stepping into a different realm altogether.

Apart from that, everything else was smooth and well‑managed. Ticket booking was hassle‑free, the staff was courteous and helpful, and the cleanliness of the entire area was commendable.

A heartfelt thank you to the staff for maintaining such a serene and refreshing space.

featured_reviews.name: Aswin Ashok
featured_reviews.review_text: It is very neat and clean, with a calm and pleasant atmosphere. Taxis are easily available. Best time to visit is 6:30–7:30 am or 6–7 pm. Book your slot in advance. There was a small queue in the early morning around 6:30 am, but it was well managed.

featured_reviews.name: Kanak Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Firstly it was a lil' confusing to get to the location. As we got off from the Churchgate and took a Cab for the trail. The map was not accurate at navigating.

As soon as we reached the main gate, there was a small alley with a small grocery store for snacks purpose leading towards the start point for the walking trail and a path which led to the Girgaon Chowpatty.

You need to purchase a ticket of Rs.25 per head. They have slots of half hour for each grp of visitors. After every half hour a new batch of fixed visitors are allowed to enter.

The guards who I talked to was not helpful to tell the entry procedure and figured out by self.

The walk is very pleasant, surrounded by trees amidst the Malabar Hill with a mesmerizing view of sea line.
The walk is not that long.

Overall the purpose was served just the accessibility was the issue.

featured_reviews.name: Swapnil Thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
Nice forest walk garden. although it is small around 1 km round to round , its good experience.
Entrance is though small galli, no space for parking near it. nearest you can park is near hanging garden which is 5-10 mins walk.

we visited at 9am and experience was good. we didnt spot any birds, except crows.
got to know from other people that view is good in evenings who likes lights and city skyline and in early mornings.
Adding photos for 9am which also looks nice.
People generally come for photography.
Gaurds are strict and will ask to move out when time slots ends. so reach sharp at starting of slot to spend more time and photography.

There is hanging garden also nearby it which people can visit.

featured_reviews.name: Manish Yadav
featured_reviews.review_text:
This 485-meter elevated walkway is a refreshing change of pace for South Mumbai. Walking through the canopy of a 12-acre forest feels like you’ve been transported out of the city, even with the skyscrapers still visible through the trees.
​The wooden deck is well-maintained, and the markings on the railings add a great touch. They identify the flora and mention elusive wildlife like the Indian Rock Python and the Great Indian Hornbill, which are rare treats to spot if you’re lucky enough.
